rationale: All four lenses plus the standards audit ran clean against a present spec; 7 findings survive triage as unambiguous major-severity patches on newly-introduced code (no defer, no decision_needed) — DesktopTelemetryRuntime never sums tokens for desktop-detected sessions, a corrupt metrics-delta line aborts the whole session-end metrics send (not just tokens), the native-loader ownership scan has no fallback past its 256KB budget, unvalidated numeric token coercion in claude.metrics-processor.ts, analytics export omitting the new cost/active-duration fields, and two test-coverage gaps (activeDurationMs passthrough, non-report cost enrichment). 7 other lens-flagged concerns were dismissed after verifying the surrounding code already handles them (cost-enricher.ts already isolates per-session failures with try/catch; the per-agent token gate and dual incremental/cumulative token reporting are confirmed intentional by spec.md) or found speculative/below the emission floor. Standards review passed clean with no coverage gap.

standards_review.notes: All 8 commit subjects match <type>(<scope>): <subject>; types/scopes are in commitlint.config.cjs enum; subjects imperative, under 100 chars.
Exported functions have explicit return types, .js imports, interfaces, JSDoc. No new console.log/require(). Pre-existing oversized files only get small additive blocks.
No attribution-header/JWT paths touched. New token-count fields are non-sensitive telemetry logged via logger.debug/info. No secrets, unsanitized paths, or header/cookie logging introduced.

findings.title: Unvalidated numeric token usage fields
findings.problem: usage.input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_read_input_tokens/cache_creation_input_tokens are used directly via `?? 0` without numeric coercion; completedMsg.message.usage is read from an untyped transcript entry with no runtime guard against non-numeric values.
findings.impact: A non-numeric usage value would flow into delta.tokens, and downstream `+=` summation in hook.ts and metrics-aggregator.ts would silently coerce into string concatenation, corrupting all downstream token totals for that session with no error surfaced. Reachability from a live malformed transcript is unconfirmed since Anthropic API responses are normally well-typed, so this is a defensive-coding gap rather than an observed failure.
findings.recommendation: Coerce with `Number(usage.input_tokens) || 0` (and the other three fields) before building the tokens object.

findings.title: No test coverage for activeDurationMs passthrough
findings.problem: activeDurationMs is read in data-loader.ts, passed through aggregator.ts into SessionAnalytics, and rendered by formatter.ts's 'Active:' line, but no test in the chain asserts the field is present or correctly rendered.
findings.impact: A regression that drops or miscomputes activeDurationMs in the aggregator would silently remove or corrupt the 'Active:' console line on every codemie analytics invocation, and no existing test would catch it — aggregator.test.ts and data-loader.test.ts never reference activeDurationMs, and no formatter test exists.
findings.recommendation: Add an aggregator test asserting sessionAnalytics[0].activeDurationMs matches the raw session value, and/or a formatter test asserting the 'Active:' line renders correctly.

findings.title: Cost and active duration missing from analytics export
findings.problem: --export json/csv serialize the plain analytics (RootAnalytics) tree, which never receives the costIndex/costSummary merge that the console path uses; exportCSV's fixed column list also has no Active Duration or Cost column at all.
findings.impact: The Est. Cost / per-session Cost values now shown on every console run (and, for CSV, activeDurationMs) are silently absent from exported files, so a user exporting a report for further analysis gets an inconsistent, incomplete dataset compared to what they just saw on screen.
findings.recommendation: Merge costIndex/costSummary into the exported payload before exportJSON, and add Active Duration / Cost columns to exportCSV.

findings.title: No test for cost enrichment on the non-report path
findings.problem: Cost enrichment now runs unconditionally in runAnalytics (previously only when wantReport), but no test calls runAnalytics without report/reportFormat/reportOutput/open set; every case in analytics-cli-metadata.test.ts passes report: true.
findings.impact: A regression that makes cost enrichment conditional again (e.g. reverting to `else if (wantReport)`) would silently stop showing 'Est. Cost'/'Cost:' lines for the majority of invocations — the plain codemie analytics command — while the full existing test suite keeps passing.
findings.recommendation: Add a test calling runAnalytics with no report flags asserting enrichCosts (or the AnalyticsFormatter cost constructor args) was invoked.

findings.title: Ownership-marker scan has no fallback past 256KB
findings.problem: hasOwnershipMarker's bounded scan reads a fixed 262,144-byte budget looking for the codemie_session_start marker line, with no fallback or logging when the marker still falls beyond that budget.
findings.impact: This raise from 4KB to 256KB fixes the specific 153-session regression observed, but a hookAdditionalContext blob larger than the new budget would reproduce the exact same 'misreported as native-external' bug this change targets, at a higher size threshold, with nothing to detect or flag the recurrence.
findings.recommendation: When bytesRead === SCAN_BYTES and no marker was found, fall back to a full-file line scan (or log a warning) instead of returning false outright.

findings.title: Corrupt metrics-delta line aborts session-end metrics entirely
findings.problem: MetricsWriter.readAll() re-throws on a single unparseable JSONL line (e.g. from a crash mid-append); hook.ts's sendSessionEndMetrics awaits readAll() with no local try/catch, so that exception propagates out of the whole function body.
findings.impact: The outer catch in sendSessionEndMetrics logs a warning and swallows the error, but by then the entire session-end metrics send has been skipped — not just token totals, but status, duration, and everything else that call would have reported — for one corrupted delta line. This goes beyond the explicit 'missing/empty file' resilience requirement and silently drops a session's telemetry.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the per-line JSON.parse in MetricsWriter.readAll() (or the call site) so a single malformed line is skipped/logged rather than aborting the whole read.

findings.title: Desktop-detected sessions never get token totals
findings.problem: DesktopTelemetryRuntime.sendSessionEndMetric calls sender.sendSessionEnd(...) with undefined for the tokens argument; unlike hook.ts's session-end path, it never sums the session's MetricsWriter deltas before sending.
findings.impact: A Claude Desktop session that ends via this poller (rather than the CLI SessionEnd hook) never reports input/output/cache token totals at all, silently diverging from the CLI path's cumulative token metric with no signal that this caller was left behind.
findings.recommendation: Sum MetricsWriter(session.sessionId).readAll() tokens in sendSessionEndMetric, mirroring hook.ts's sendSessionEndMetrics, before calling sendSessionEnd.
